text:
deploy-bot: Scheduled deploy: staging -> prod at 2024-04-03 02:00 UTC. Includes migration 20240403_add_user_flags and backfill job.
jordan: FYI this migration adds a nullable column + backfill over users table (~120M rows). backfill estimated 2-3 hours if we throttle. requires advisory lock to avoid double writes.
eva: we should run the schema change first (no blocking), then run backfill as a separate job to avoid long locks. plan: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN (NULL); then feature-flag writes only after backfill.
mike: +1. we need to pin api-server image on the deploy so we can rollback easily. i'll create a release tag and put it in the release notes.
raj: question: do we need to put a write lock during the backfill? risk of inconsistent reads if consumer reads before backfill finishes.
sarah: we can keep writes on, but funnel new flags behind feature flag. backfill will fill historical rows. we only need a short exclusive lock for the ALTER if Postgres requires it — using ADD COLUMN with DEFAULT and without lock trick is dangerous. use: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN user_flags JSONB; then run UPDATE in batches.
jordan: deployment window is 02:00-06:00 UTC. oncall will cover the first 2 hours; we should notify customers in the change window note.
oncall-bot: @oncall paged: oncall rotation for 2024-04-03 02:00 UTC -> 2024-04-03 06:00 UTC.
mike: backfill script: scripts/backfill_user_flags.sh --batch-size=5000 --sleep-ms=200. run as k8s Job in dedicated namespace so it doesn't compete with web pods.
raj: please add a DB kill switch and a rollback plan: if backfill causes replication lag > 3min or CPU > 80% for > 10m, we abort and revert reads to replica.
eva: added health checks and canary percent: deploy will rollout to 10% instances for 15min, then 50%, then 100%. pin tag: redwood/api-server@20240403-migration.
jordan: i'm going to attach release notes and the migration runbook in the PR. includes commands to resume/abort backfill.
mike: stash of rollback steps in case of catastrophic failure: 1) scale down new canary pods 2) revert deploy tag to redwood/api-server@20240328-stable 3) stop backfill job 4) restore from replica snapshot if necessary.
sarah: small nit: ensure the ALTER uses "ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS" so retried deploys are idempotent.
raj: we'll also set a lock via advisory lock before starting update batches: SELECT pg_advisory_lock(123456); and release after each batch with pg_advisory_unlock. add deadlock watchdog.
eva: scheduling note: request DBA to increase checkpoint_timeout to 10min for the window, reduces IO. assigned to @dba (cc: @sarah).
(12:50) jordan: I'm going to tag the PR and kick off the dry-run on staging tonight.
(13:20) deploy-bot: dry-run succeeded on staging: migration + backfill simulated with sample 10M rows. no schema conflicts. logs: https://ci.redwood/example/1234
(20:05) mike: oncall approved the plan. added Grafana panels for replication lag and write latency; alert thresholds set.
(21:00) sarah: added runbook snippet: ```bash
# abort backfill
kubectl -n migrations delete job user-flags-backfill
psql -h writer -c "SELECT pg_cancel_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE query LIKE '%UPDATE users SET user_flags%';"
```
jordan: final checklist: 1) tag pinned images 2) create release notes 3) DB advisor + DBA approval 4) runbook uploaded to Confluence 5) notify support & customers 6) start within window.
mike: i'll post release note bluntly in #announcements once deploy is green.
jordan: starting deploy at 02:00 UTC. if anything goes wrong we use the rollback steps above. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
